Adopt's start runs run's shared start, refuses before any log or child, and logs as `process:"run"` with `instance:<ViolaName>`. Any record this chunk adds for an early child exit (event or log line) carries that identity, and the start's refusal order stays as written.

**2026-11-24-viola-adopt** (§8, 4 rows, 1 of 2) — ~ decision/strict-modes-refusal-before-any-write, ~ contract/json-fault/internal-error, ~ decision/socket-dir-refusal-before-any-frame and ~ decision/claude-agents-read-fails-open gained adopt's start and preflight. Adopt stays silent at the internal-error catch site like run and revive's start. A new early-exit outcome has to fit beside these lists and must not break the "silent there" rule for a start.

**2026-11-24-viola-adopt** (§8, 2 rows, 2 of 2) — ~ contract/cli-fixed-message/form and ~ contract/start-json-refusal/document: adopt's own strict-modes-failed and session-live refusals print the fixed `unable:` / `hint:` pair, and under `--json` they give one `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` document with no hint. A new closed word for "the resumed child ended at once" extends these two closed lists, in both the human form and the `--json` form.

**2026-11-24-viola-adopt** (§1 and §2, 1 row each) — ~ contract/tui-passthrough/entry: a passthrough is entered by a viola adopt whose preflight passed. ~ contract/cli-refusal/unable-line: adopt's two own refusals are one-line `unable:` forms. A child that exits right after the start may already have held the terminal, so the zero-viola-bytes boundary decides whether any line can be printed at all. If the chunk prints one, the unable-line list gains a third adopt form.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (revive --json documents every refusal of its start) — this set contract/viola-revive-json/start-refusal and contract/tui-passthrough/pump-child-error / contract/viola-revive-json/pump-child-error: a `pump_child` error prints no document, because the child has held the terminal and viola writes nothing past it. This is the main trap for the early-exit word. Anything said after the child started breaks that boundary unless it is moved before the hand-over or recorded off-terminal only.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (a lost wrapper and a stale holder each read their own code) — added contract/start-holder-refusal/already-live and contract/start-holder-refusal/stale-heartbeat: stale heartbeat is exit 1's cause alone. Whether adopt releases the instance directory and name after an early exit decides which of these codes the next start or re-adopt reads.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (a name with no endpoint reads the instance directory) — added contract/instance-unreachable-detail/instance-dead (the directory stands) and contract/instance-unreachable-detail/unwrapped-name (no directory). If the instance directory is kept after an early exit, frame verbs read `instance-dead`. If it is released, they read `unwrapped-name`. The chunk's release choice decides which one users see.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (the exit-cause table and one hint per code) — `no_two_codes_share_a_hint` and `no_hint_names_release` in `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` (decision/one-hint-per-code, decision/no-hint-names-release). **2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (the `unwrapped-name` and `endpoint-lost` hints and their pins) — precedent for a new hint: it ends with its own `hint:` as the last stderr line, in plain ASCII, naming only the parsed ViolaName (decision/printed-names-are-parsed-arguments), and it is pinned by `send_hint_is_the_design_string` and the exit-cause table.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (the `cli` catch site's `internal-error` document) — this set contract/json-fault/internal-error: run's, revive's (and later adopt's) start stays silent there. A new early-exit word is the same kind of widening and needs the same word from the operator.

body: The spawn folder of the adopt start: the folder the resumed claude child is started in, chosen so the CLI finds the adopted session.

A new early-exit outcome of `viola adopt`: when the resumed child ends right after the start, viola prints a refusal of the CLI refusal format, an unable line with a plain word and its kebab-case reason code beside it, then a hint line, on stderr in the refusal stderr layout.
The exit code that early exit returns, taken from the CLI exit-code table, never the child's bare exit status passed through as error text.
The new code word's hint: exactly one hint per code, the refusal ends with it, no hint names release; if the outcome is a fault instead, it carries no hint.
Under --json the early exit is one clean failure document with no hint and no stray bytes, of the same shape as the other start refusal documents.
The new fixed strings (unable word, code, hint, output line) come from the design copy and are pinned by literal in tests; the error message interpolates nothing.
Refusal and failure words of the new outcome carry no colour and no SGR; no SGR off a terminal or in plain modes.
Any value the new output line or hint could carry (a folder, a session id) is not printed as a path, and any control byte reaching CLI output is printed escaped.
The recorded event and log line for the early exit: the event line form and the log identity tags (process, service name); run diagnostics go to the log, never to the terminal.
The terminal while the resumed child runs and after it ends belongs to the child: viola writes no bytes of its own onto it during the passthrough; its refusal is printed only after the child is gone.
Telling an early exit from a normal one is a time bound that falls on the driver only, never on the human; no spinner or unwarned timeout.
The state after an early exit: whether the instance directory and the adopted name are released, said by the outcome and kept consistent with what the board and revive later read.
The R5 rig's live readings never gate CI; its rehearse form runs with no claude and is the only form a test or CI may fire.

body_fields.convention: each new a11y assertion runs inside the existing test suites as a nextest failure, never in a separate a11y driver, suite or artifact
each new test passes with no skips, no retries and zero flakiness; a gate breach fails the build
each new boundary test is sequenced on records, never on timing, and never inspects claude content

body: The `viola list` board's caption, order, colour, dim stale rows and NAME truncation: the chunk changes no board output.
`viola --help` rows (usage line, group labels, handoff row, served verbs): no verb is added or regrouped.
`viola link`/`unlink`, `viola plugin install`, `viola revive --list`, `viola switch`, `viola up`, `viola verify` and `viola wait` output contracts: other commands' lines, untouched.
MCP server frame tools, hook event and dialog calls, and frame verb refusals: the adopt start sends no frame over those channels anew.
The send and answer refusals and the dialog hold: the chunk sends no prompt and answers no dialog.
Screen-reader targets and the manual Orca and keyboard passes: supplemental, gating nothing, not owed by this fix.
Absences of a web or graphical frontend, touch surface, rendered page, i18n, and the structured-violation JSON schema: nothing of these is reached.

**2026-11-24-viola-adopt** (Established Decisions: 4 rows, amd-zqfvjh3b) — added decision/adopt-refuses-live-session (PROVISIONAL, delegate overseer) and put adopt into launch-pair-handed-not-verified, no-start-over-live-instance and run-refuses-held-name. This is the verb this chunk fixes. Adopt runs run's own start: the collision check, the holder pair and the launch pair. Any new early-exit word, and any release of the name after it, has to sit beside these refusals without breaking them.

**2026-11-24-viola-adopt** (Standard Contracts, Conventions and Occupied Resources: amd-dcpzjliq, amd-chk4orxc, amd-fb577owg, amd-mmk2jgwo, amd-oq6673zw) — these added contract/cli-json-output/adopt-refusal-codes (eight codes; only strict-modes-failed and session-live are adopt's own) and contract/cli-verbs/adopt. They also added adopt's start to the roles that stay silent at the internal-error catch site. contract/child-argv/resume and contract/claude-child-argv/resume gained an adopted start with the operator-typed id. run-<name>.ndjson names adopt's start (process `run`), and the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR read and the socket-dir-refused detail name adopt's start. A new closed word for a child that ends at once extends this code list and its role-file lines. Adopt's start stays silent at the catch site.

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** (the snapshot's `cwd` and the child's second cwd source, amd-6lmcqivl) — added the snapshot's `cwd?` (valid UTF-8 only, a host path kept only in the 0600 snapshot) and made a revived start spawn in that recorded cwd. The cwd is read after the strict-modes check and must be an existing directory, else `cwd-missing`. A replayed snapshot gives no cwd, so a revive over it is refused. Program resolution and the version gate never read it. The founder ratified the recorded directory as a spawn directory, live, as a boundary widening. This is the precedent and the trap for giving adopt a spawn folder other than the caller's: adopt has no record to read, and a new folder source would be a new crossing.

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** (revive verb registered, amd-cuhxvhre; replay reader and session chain, amd-ik5pljrk) — a revived start launches `claude` by name on its own PATH and adds `--resume <id>` as one argv element. Each preflight refusal is one unable/hint pair plus one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail}` in run-<name>.ndjson, with no recorded directory, pid or logged id. Revive resumes in place with wheel `driver`. This is the pattern adopt copies and the shape for an early-exit refusal's pair and log line.

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** (a second relied-on shape with no row, amd-vfeukntd) — `claude --resume <id>` reopening the same session with SessionStart source `resume` was measured on 2.1.287 in three live starts and is read only under the fake agent in CI. The fake agent's `--resume` builds that SessionStart unconditionally, so CI cannot tell a resume the CLI refuses from one it takes. This chunk's red R5a came from that gap.

**2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through** (four crossings ratified, amd-cizrj2th) — ratified the logged session id as the value of `--resume` on the child's command line. The id is a crossing shown to the founder. Adopt's operator-typed id rests on this precedent, so any change to how adopt passes or checks the id stays inside it.

**2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows** (resume row and Run E, amd-4oikdxwt; Run E's resources, amd-mb4bcuuw) — added the resume-session ledger row and its Run E probe. Run E runs in its own `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-resume/` folder and resumes Run B's session, which was made in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/`. The live reading on 2.1.287: «`--resume <id>` found Run B's session from Run E's own `-resume` project dir». This is the one recorded measurement of a resume from a folder other than the one the session was made in, so it bears directly on hypothesis A. Its CLI version and folder relation, a sibling under one cwd, limit how far it reaches.

**2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola** (verify's print-mode probe leaves an empty CLI project dir, amd-vdbwbrik) — measured that the CLI keeps a per-cwd project dir under `~/.claude/projects/` (a `memory/` dir, no transcript) for a print-mode session. This is evidence that the CLI keys its session store by the session's folder, which bears on both hypothesis A and hypothesis B. The reading touched the operator's real `~/.claude`, which this phase must not read.

**2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board** (revive refuses a session id live elsewhere, amd-fgwitppd) — added revive's `session-live` reading: one `claude agents --json` read, `--fork` skipping it, a failed read passing. Measured live on 2.1.287: a second `--resume` of a held id runs under the same id, two writers on one transcript. decision/adopt-refuses-live-session copies this. A fix that changes where or how adopt resumes must keep this refusal ahead of the spawn.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (revive --json documents every refusal of its start, amd-l6vcl476) — closed the post-preflight gap: every refusal of the start prints the refused document before `spawn_child`. «a `pump_child` error prints no document, because the child has held the terminal» was kept, and contract/revive-json/pump-error and decision/no-document-after-child-held-terminal state it. This is the binding trap for this chunk: a resumed child that ends at once has already held the terminal, so what adopt says and records then cannot be a --json refusal document unless that rule is revisited.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (`stale-heartbeat`, amd-lqa2vdge; the code-word rule and the exit-cause table, amd-weptokca) — each exit-1 cause carries its own code word. Every exit-1 code must pass `is_code_word` and stand as a row of `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs`, and `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` checks that no two codes share a hint. A new early-exit word and its hint must enter both tables.

**2026-10-10-budget-governor** (the instance check before any log, amd-aidtawel) — made revive's start arm run `check_instance` before its wrapper log opens. Opening a log narrows an existing home to 0700, so a check after it passed a widened home. A refused check writes no line, and the Epoch 5 batch (2026-10-20T06-58-31-wrap) accepted that as built. This is the order adopt's start inherits: any new record of an early exit comes after these checks and must not open a log before them.

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** (one read per revive, amd-d7zf6zxp; home-tree check before the start's log, amd-2esr3nid) — a revive's preflight reads the snapshot once and passes that read to its collision check and its recorded-directory reading (decision/revive-reads-snapshot-once, one state-recovered line). Every start runs `check_home_tree` through `checked_exe` before its log, and a refusal is exit 1 with no line. If adopt gains a recorded or chosen folder, the same one-read and check-first constraints apply.

**2026-11-18-session-folder-trusted-by-viola** (amd-s4susov6, amd-bsqfib5j, amd-peqz77j5; ratified 2026-11-22T17-29-41Z-wrap) — on a verified CLI a start writes the trust record of an untrusted spawn folder, keyed in the child's Claude config by the spawn directory. Revive keys its record by the recorded cwd (contract/instance-snapshot/cwd, decision/spawn-directory-confined-to-snapshot). Changing adopt's spawn folder changes which folder gets a trust record written into the user's Claude config, and the host path may appear nowhere else.

**2026-11-17-trust-record-ledger-row** (the trust-record row's rule reworded, amd-j3qjnbcq) — the row asks per CLI version whether a written trust record opens the folder with no modal. The one live reading, on 2.1.325, read fail. Spawning adopt's child in a new folder can bring up the folder-trust modal even with a record written. A child that sits on that modal looks different from one that ends at once, and the early-exit reading must tell them apart.

**2026-11-20-a-new-cli-version-stamped-automatically** (run-start-order, amd-m6kilzox) — fixed the start order: resolve, collision check, pin, version gate, bind, automatic verify, trust record on a verified verdict, first snapshot, heartbeat and events, then the spawn last. Adopt's start runs this order. Any spawn-folder choice must be made before the trust step and the first snapshot, and an early exit comes after the snapshot and start events are already written.

**2026-11-24-viola-up** (cwd readers, amd-5j2lz4ky, ratified by amd-ek3pttsh; up-selection-rule, amd-lxnfy53i) — `viola up` reads the recorded cwd and opens each terminal there. It re-opens a gone instance only when its heartbeat predates the boot and, unless named, its log has no session-end after its last session-start. What adopt records for a child that ends at once (a session-end or not, a cwd or not), and whether the instance directory stays, decides whether `up` later tries to revive a dead adopted instance.

**2026-11-24-switching-a-session-s-model-and-effort** (amd-47claoze, amd-2dezy377, amd-7szmmph3, amd-xo4jntnv) — a switch respawns the child with `--resume` of the same id. Its refusals added the closed not-delivered details `child-not-ended` and `resume-failed`, and the late session-end of the switched id is dropped once (PROVISIONAL, delegate overseer). This is the nearest precedent for naming a resume the CLI does not take, and for screening a late session-end. A word for adopt's early exit should be weighed against `resume-failed` so the closed sets do not split one cause.

**2026-11-23-model-and-effort-at-launch** (amd-tygcu36s, amd-quxrv25i, amd-mzho2hbo) — every start hands a model and effort pair that is never verified. It appends a log-only `launch` line, and the snapshot holds `launch?`. A revive replays the recorded pair. An adopted child that ends at once has already appended these lines, so the record left behind holds a launch with no session.

**2026-09-25-pty-wrapper-on-windows** (explicit child cwd, amd-clwmgl5z) — recorded the as-built explicit child cwd: the child's cwd is set explicitly to viola's current directory. This is the origin of decision/child-cwd-explicit, whose only exception is revive's recorded cwd. Moving adopt's spawn folder off the caller's directory adds a second exception to this row.

Hints never quote text or name paths: the early-exit hint must not quote the child's output nor name the spawn folder or any session file path.

CLI --json mode as one document: under --json the early-exit outcome is a single refusal document with its code, never mixed with human lines.
Human output is a contract and words carry every state: the early-exit line is fixed wording pinned by tests, its state carried by a word and never by colour alone.

A CLI target is always a ViolaName, never case-transformed: the --name given to adopt is kept as given across the early-exit path and its output line.
No interactive prompt, no spinner, no progress glyph: an early exit is reported once, after the child ended, with no waiting animation and no question asked.

body: The adopt start's resumed claude child gets a new spawn folder; the adopt start keeps logging as run, with the claude-child process-start and process-exit lines in the run process log.

A new early-exit cause of viola adopt gets its own closed detail code, distinct from every other exit-1 cause of adopt, carrying no path or pid: one more entry in the process-exit detail codes for exit 1 from viola adopt.
The early child exit is read from the process handle, never from screen content; its exit code and duration ride the claude-child process-exit line as typed fields.
The early exit reaches the human as a fixed, pathless stderr unable/hint pair beside the existing refusal pairs; the error message interpolates nothing, no session id and no folder.
The early exit is recorded as a product event in the events log: a closed event value, the event line shape kept, emission deterministic, and no event payload copied into the process log.
Any new event word, detail word or field added to the diagnostics line is additive only and joins the diagnostic line schema and its closed enums, so the schema matches the event enum.
Adopt's typed session id is never logged; the resume folder path appears in no home-level line or detail code, at most in the instance detail file.
The instance is resolved from its name, never from the working directory: moving the child's spawn folder must not change how adopt finds or names its instance, nor which diagnostics files it writes.
Releasing or keeping the instance directory and the name after the early exit follows the rule that no process log is written without an instance and that a refused check opens no process log.
The CLAUDE environment strip and identity floor still apply to the resumed child at its new folder; stripped values are never logged, names only.
Wrapped claude internals and Claude Code transcripts are not a contract: the product must not decide the resume folder by reading the CLI's transcript store.
The capability ledger is read for a row on resume from another folder (none means UNMEASURED); an unreadable ledger counts as unverified, and the ledger's path and stamps are never logged.
Every new log line goes through the single obs_event macro with explicit corr and instance; no raw tracing macros, no print macros, and an instrument attribute skips all arguments.
The early-exit and spawn-folder behaviour is proved against the fake agent only; the real CLI never runs in CI or in this phase, and the rig's rehearse arm spawns no claude.
The revive and up starts' resume folder (the snapshot's recorded cwd, with the cwd-missing exit-1 detail) is read as the model for adopt's folder, never changed.

body: The resume folder of an adopt start: the resumed claude child is spawned in the folder the CLI finds the adopted session from, no longer the caller's current directory; a test asserts the folder the child actually started in (as the fake agent's receipt records its cwd), never the product's own claim.

How revive and up choose their resume folder — the instance snapshot's recorded cwd, read through the snapshot read-or-replay path, a replayed snapshot carrying no cwd — and that adopt alone has no such record; the adopt fix must take its folder from a source of its own and refuse, not guess, where that folder is missing, as revive's cwd-missing refusal does.

A new closed refusal word for a resumed child that ends at once, added beside the existing start and revive refusal tables (run and revive exit 1 causes, revive refusal codes): its exit code, its own hint naming its cause, its human line and its --json failure document; a closed word changes only by decision.

The early-exit detection itself: the child's exit is read on the process handle by waiting on it, never on PTY EOF, and an exit right after the start is told apart from a normal later end of the session.

What an early exit of the adopted child records: the event log record and the process-exit log line, their fields and corr, each line JSON per line in the process log format, with no secret, no session transcript text and no upstream child output beyond what the contract allows.

Whether the instance directory and the name are released after an early exit, so a second adopt or a run of the same name is not refused as already-live, squatted-name or stale-heartbeat afterwards; asserted on the files and liveness viola reads, not on a hand-written state file.

The new hint and error body hold no path, no folder name and no upstream text, though the fix is about a folder; human output escapes control characters and carries no SGR without a terminal; one JSON document per verb run.

The claude child spawn of adopt keeps the child environment strip and the process-start claude-child record (env kept, stripped counts) unchanged while its folder changes; the child is still given its viola name, instance dir and binary.

Tests prove the fix only against the fake agent serving the claude boundary, with a fake agent that exits at once (its exit trigger) standing in for the real child's early exit; no real claude CLI in tests or CI, and a fake-agent run is no proof of real-CLI resume behaviour.

Tests never read the host's claude sessions or real config; each adopt test runs under a test-owned user home and creates its own sessions, and the trust-start folders a test spawns the child in lie outside any repository.

The R5 rig change, if any: the live arm types the command in the folder the fix requires; its --rehearse form reaches the changed path with no claude; the rig's seams stay rehearse-only, it runs clean of the firing session with its root outside every repository, and its screen read takes the compiled shapes only.

Real adopt stays proven only by the gated live reading R5 of the adopt chunk; this chunk adds no live step, and a live reading is recorded as a reading, never as verification; the chunk claims no capability.
The capability ledger as re-read for a resume from another folder: no row means UNMEASURED and is said so; the version gate and stamps are not widened by this chunk to claim a resume capability.
